title: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring Trend
scenario: A 29-year-old client at 39 weeks gestation is in active labor with continuous external fetal monitoring. The nurse reviews the fetal heart rate pattern recorded over the last hour.

questions.subject: Maternity
questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the change in the fetal heart rate pattern over the last hour?

options.text: A reassuring pattern that has become non-reassuring
A consistently reassuring pattern requiring no change
An expected pattern of fetal head compression only
A pattern indicating imminent normal delivery

questions.rationale: The tracing moved from moderate variability with no decelerations to minimal variability with recurrent late decelerations, indicating uteroplacental insufficiency and a non-reassuring (Category II/III) pattern.

questions.subject: Maternity
questions.stem: Recognizing the recurrent late decelerations, select the 3 priority nursing interventions.

options.text: Reposition the client to a lateral position
Increase the rate of the IV fluid infusion
Document the finding and continue routine monitoring

questions.rationale: Intrauterine resuscitation for recurrent late decelerations includes lateral repositioning, oxygen administration, and an IV fluid bolus to improve placental perfusion. Oxytocin should be stopped, not increased.
